title: Mechanical Properties of Solids
syllabus: Elastic behaviour, Stress-strain relationship, Hooke's law, Young's modulus, bulk modulus, modulus of rigidity, Poisson's ratio; Elastic potential energy stored in a stretched wire, work done in stretching a wire

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] Two wires $A$ and $B$ are made of the same material. Wire $A$ has length $L$ and radius $r$, while wire $B$ has length $2L$ and radius $2r$. If both are subjected to the same stretching force, the ratio of the elongation produced in wire $A$ to that in wire $B$ is:
questions.solution:
Elongation $\Delta L$ is given by $\Delta L = \frac{F L}{A Y} = \frac{F L}{\pi r^2 Y}$.
For identical material ($Y$) and equal tension force ($F$):
$$\Delta L \propto \frac{L}{r^2}$$
$$\frac{\Delta L_A}{\Delta L_B} = \left(\frac{L_A}{L_B}\right) \left(\frac{r_B}{r_A}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{L}{2L}\right) \left(\frac{2r}{r}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 4 = 2$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] The stress-strain curves for two materials $A$ and $B$ are plotted. Material $A$ has a greater slope in the elastic region and a wide plastic deformation region before fracture, whereas material $B$ has a smaller slope and breaks immediately past its elastic limit. Which statement is correct?
options: Material $A$ is more ductile and has greater Young's modulus than $B$
Material $B$ is more ductile and has greater Young's modulus than $A$
Material $A$ is brittle and has lower Young's modulus than $B$
Material $B$ is ductile and has greater tensile strength
questions.solution:
Young's modulus equals the slope of the stress-strain graph in the linear elastic regime; thus, $Y_A > Y_B$.
A large plastic deformation region between the yield point and breaking point corresponds to a ductile material, whereas breaking shortly after the elastic limit signifies brittleness.
Therefore, material $A$ has a greater Young's modulus and is ductile.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A uniform metal wire of length $L$, cross-sectional area $A$, and density $\rho$ hangs vertically under its own weight. If Young's modulus of the material is $Y$, the total elongation of the wire is:
questions.solution:
Consider an element of length $dy$ at distance $y$ from the bottom free end.
Tension at height $y$ is the weight of the segment below it: $T(y) = (A y \rho) g$.
Elongation of element: $d(\Delta L) = \frac{T(y) dy}{A Y} = \frac{\rho g y dy}{Y}$.
Integrating from $y = 0$ to $y = L$:
$$\Delta L = \int_0^L \frac{\rho g y}{Y} dy = \frac{\rho g L^2}{2Y}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] When a rubber cord of cross-sectional area $A$ and original length $L$ is stretched by length $\Delta L$, the elastic potential energy density stored in the cord is:
questions.solution:
Total elastic energy stored in a stretched wire is $U = \frac{1}{2} F \Delta L$.
Energy density (energy per unit volume $V = A L$) is:
$$u = \frac{U}{V} = \frac{\frac{1}{2} F \Delta L}{A L} = \frac{1}{2} \left(\frac{F}{A}\right) \left(\frac{\Delta L}{L}\right) = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{Stress} \times \text{Strain}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A metallic sphere of volume $V$ is taken from the surface to a depth $h$ in a lake where the water pressure is $P$. If the bulk modulus of the metal is $B$, the fractional decrease in its volume $\left(-\frac{\Delta V}{V}\right)$ is:
questions.solution:
Bulk modulus $B$ is defined by the ratio of volumetric stress (excess pressure $\Delta P = P$) to volumetric strain:
$$B = -\frac{\Delta P}{\Delta V / V} \implies -\frac{\Delta V}{V} = \frac{P}{B}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2019] If the Poisson's ratio of a material is $\sigma = 0.2$ and a longitudinal strain of $4.0 \times 10^{-3}$ is produced in a wire of this material, the lateral strain produced is:
questions.solution:
Poisson's ratio is defined as the negative ratio of lateral strain to longitudinal strain:
$$\sigma = -\frac{\text{Lateral Strain}}{\text{Longitudinal Strain}}$$
$$\text{Lateral Strain} = -\sigma \times (\text{Longitudinal Strain}) = -0.2 \times (4.0 \times 10^{-3}) = -8.0 \times 10^{-4}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A steel wire of length $2\text{ m}$ and cross-sectional area $2\text{ mm}^2$ is clamped rigidly between two fixed supports at temperature $30^\circ\text{C}$. If the temperature falls to $10^\circ\text{C}$, the thermal tension developed in the wire is (take coefficient of linear expansion $\alpha = 1.2 \times 10^{-5}\text{ }^\circ\text{C}^{-1}$ and $Y = 2 \times 10^{11}\text{ N/m}^2$):
questions.solution:
Temperature decrease $\Delta T = 30 - 10 = 20^\circ\text{C}$.
Thermal strain prevented by fixed supports is $\frac{\Delta L}{L} = \alpha \Delta T$.
Thermal stress: $\frac{F}{A} = Y \alpha \Delta T$.
Tension force:
$$F = Y A \alpha \Delta T = (2 \times 10^{11}) \times (2 \times 10^{-6}) \times (1.2 \times 10^{-5}) \times 20$$
$$F = 4 \times 10^5 \times 2.4 \times 10^{-4} = 96\text{ N}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] The relation between Young's modulus $Y$, Bulk modulus $B$, and Modulus of rigidity $\eta$ for an isotropic elastic solid is given by:
questions.solution:
The standard elastic modulus relations involving Poisson's ratio $\sigma$ are $Y = 3B(1 - 2\sigma)$ and $Y = 2\eta(1 + \sigma)$.
Eliminating $\sigma$ between them:
$$1 - 2\sigma = \frac{Y}{3B} \implies 2\sigma = 1 - \frac{Y}{3B}$$
$$1 + \sigma = \frac{Y}{2\eta} \implies 2\sigma = \frac{Y}{\eta} - 2$$
$$1 - \frac{Y}{3B} = \frac{Y}{\eta} - 2 \implies 3 = Y\left(\frac{1}{3B} + \frac{1}{\eta}\right)$$
Dividing by $Y$ and multiplying by 3 yields:
$$\frac{9}{Y} = \frac{1}{B} + \frac{3}{\eta}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] A wire suspended vertically from one of its ends is stretched by attaching a weight of $200\text{ N}$ to the lower end. The weight stretches the wire by $1\text{ mm}$. The work done in stretching the wire is:
questions.solution:
Work done in stretching an elastic wire by a gradually increasing load $F$ is:
$$W = \frac{1}{2} F \Delta L = \frac{1}{2} \times 200\text{ N} \times (1 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}) = 0.1\text{ J}$$
Note: The potential energy lost by the hanging weight is $F \Delta L = 0.2\text{ J}$, but half of it ($0.1\text{ J}$) is dissipated as heat during internal damping.

questions.question: A cylindrical wire of radius $r$ and length $L$ is fixed at one end and twisted by an angle $\theta$ at the other end. The restoring couple produced in the wire is proportional to:
questions.solution:
The torsional couple per unit twist (torsional rigidity) of a solid cylinder of shear modulus $\eta$ is:
$$C = \frac{\pi \eta r^4}{2L}$$
Restoring couple $\tau = C \theta = \frac{\pi \eta r^4 \theta}{2L} \propto \frac{r^4}{L}$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A load of $4.0\text{ kg}$ is suspended from a ceiling through a steel wire of length $20\text{ m}$ and radius $2.0\text{ mm}$. If Young's modulus of steel is $2.0 \times 10^{11}\text{ N/m}^2$, the increase in length of the wire is (take $g = 3.14\pi\text{ m/s}^2 \approx 9.87\text{ m/s}^2$, and $\pi \approx 3.14$):
questions.solution:
Cross-sectional area $A = \pi r^2 = \pi (2 \times 10^{-3})^2 = 4\pi \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^2$.
Tensile force $F = mg = 4 \times 10 = 40\text{ N}$ (or $4 \times 9.87 \approx 39.5\text{ N}$).
$$\Delta L = \frac{F L}{A Y} = \frac{40 \times 20}{(4\pi \times 10^{-6}) \times (2.0 \times 10^{11})} = \frac{800}{8\pi \times 10^5} = \frac{1}{\pi \times 10^3}\text{ m} \approx \frac{1}{3.14}\text{ mm} \approx 0.318\text{ mm} \approx 0.32\text{ mm}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2019] For an incompressible liquid, the theoretical value of Poisson's ratio is:
questions.solution:
For a cylinder of volume $V = \pi r^2 L$:
$$\frac{\Delta V}{V} = \frac{\Delta L}{L} + 2\frac{\Delta r}{r} = \text{longitudinal strain} - 2\sigma (\text{longitudinal strain}) = (1 - 2\sigma)\frac{\Delta L}{L}$$
For an incompressible substance, $\Delta V = 0$ under any deformation:
$$1 - 2\sigma = 0 \implies \sigma = 0.5$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A uniform cube is subjected to a uniform hydrostatic pressure $P$. If the fractional change in each side of the cube is $\alpha$, then the bulk modulus of the material of the cube is:
questions.solution:
Volume of a cube of edge length $x$ is $V = x^3$.
Fractional change in volume: $\frac{\Delta V}{V} = 3\frac{\Delta x}{x} = 3(-\alpha) = -3\alpha$.
Bulk modulus:
$$B = -\frac{P}{\Delta V / V} = -\frac{P}{-3\alpha} = \frac{P}{3\alpha}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A wire of length $L$ and cross-sectional area $A$ is made of a material of Young's modulus $Y$. If the wire is stretched by an amount $x$, the required work done is:
questions.solution:
The effective spring constant of the wire is $k = \frac{Y A}{L}$.
Work done to stretch it by extension $x$ is:
$$W = \frac{1}{2} k x^2 = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{Y A}{L}\right)x^2 = \frac{Y A x^2}{2L}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] The compressiblity of water is $4 \times 10^{-5}\text{ atm}^{-1}$. The fractional decrease in volume of $100\text{ cm}^3$ of water under an external pressure of $100\text{ atm}$ is:
questions.solution:
Compressibility $K$ is the reciprocal of bulk modulus: $K = \frac{1}{B} = -\frac{\Delta V / V}{P}$.
$$-\frac{\Delta V}{V} = K \cdot P = (4 \times 10^{-5}\text{ atm}^{-1}) \times (100\text{ atm}) = 4 \times 10^{-3}$$

questions.question: A mild steel wire has a breaking stress of $S$. If the wire is cut into two equal halves, the breaking stress of each half will be:
questions.solution:
Breaking stress is an intensive intrinsic property of the material and does not depend on the length or dimensions of the specimen.
Hence, each half retains the same breaking stress $S$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A composite rod made of copper and steel sections having identical cross-sections is subjected to a tensile pull. If the length of copper is $1\text{ m}$ and steel is $1.5\text{ m}$, and $Y_{\text{copper}} = 1.0 \times 10^{11}\text{ N/m}^2$, $Y_{\text{steel}} = 2.0 \times 10^{11}\text{ N/m}^2$, the ratio of elongation of copper to steel is:
questions.solution:
Since both sections are in series, they experience the same tensile force $F$ and have identical area $A$:
$$\Delta L = \frac{F L}{A Y} \implies \Delta L \propto \frac{L}{Y}$$
$$\frac{\Delta L_{\text{Cu}}}{\Delta L_{\text{Steel}}} = \left(\frac{L_{\text{Cu}}}{L_{\text{Steel}}}\right) \left(\frac{Y_{\text{Steel}}}{Y_{\text{Cu}}}\right) = \left(\frac{1.0}{1.5}\right) \left(\frac{2.0 \times 10^{11}}{1.0 \times 10^{11}}\right) = \frac{2}{3} \times 2 = \frac{4}{3}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A solid cylinder of radius $R$ is subjected to pure shear stress $\tau$. The shear strain produced at the outer surface is:
questions.solution:
By Hooke's law in shear, shear stress is directly proportional to shear strain $\theta$ via the shear modulus (modulus of rigidity $\eta$):
$$\tau = \eta \theta \implies \theta = \frac{\tau}{\eta}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A metal ring of radius $R$ and cross-sectional area $A$ is rotated in a horizontal plane about its symmetrical vertical axis with angular speed $\omega$. If the density of the ring is $\rho$, the tensile stress developed in the ring is:
questions.solution:
Consider an infinitesimal element of the ring subtending angle $d\theta$ at the centre.
Mass of element: $dm = (R\,d\theta) A \rho$.
Centripetal force is provided by the inward components of tension $T$ at both ends:
$$2 T \sin\left(\frac{d\theta}{2}\right) \approx T d\theta = (dm) \omega^2 R = (A \rho R\,d\theta) \omega^2 R$$
$$T = A \rho \omega^2 R^2$$
Tensile stress is:
$$\sigma = \frac{T}{A} = \rho \omega^2 R^2$$

questions.question: The theoretical limits for the value of Poisson's ratio $\sigma$ for an isotropic elastic solid are:
questions.solution:
From elasticity relations $Y = 3B(1 - 2\sigma)$ and $Y = 2\eta(1 + \sigma)$:
Since elastic moduli $Y$, $B$, and $\eta$ must be positive for stability:
$1 - 2\sigma > 0 \implies \sigma < 0.5$
$1 + \sigma > 0 \implies \sigma > -1$
Hence, the theoretical range is $-1 < \sigma < 0.5$ (in practice, most solids have $0 < \sigma < 0.5$).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A steel wire of length $4.0\text{ m}$ and diameter $2.0\text{ mm}$ is stretched by a force of $200\text{ N}$. If Young's modulus of steel is $2.0 \times 10^{11}\text{ N/m}^2$, find the elongation (in mm) of the wire (take $\pi = 3.14$, rounded to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
Radius $r = 1.0\text{ mm} = 1.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}$.
Cross-sectional area $A = \pi r^2 = 3.1416 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^2$.
$$\Delta L = \frac{F L}{A Y} = \frac{200 \times 4.0}{(3.1416 \times 10^{-6}) \times (2.0 \times 10^{11})} = \frac{800}{6.2832 \times 10^5} = 1.273 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m} = 1.27\text{ mm}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] An elastic wire is stretched by $1.0\text{ mm}$ when a tension of $100\text{ N}$ is applied. Find the elastic potential energy (in Joules) stored in the stretched wire.
questions.solution:
Stored elastic energy in a stretched wire is:
$$U = \frac{1}{2} F \Delta L = \frac{1}{2} \times 100\text{ N} \times (1.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}) = 50 \times 10^{-3} = 0.05\text{ J}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A hydraulic press contains $0.5\text{ m}^3$ of oil. When the pressure on the oil is increased by $2.0 \times 10^7\text{ N/m}^2$, its volume decreases by $5.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}^3$. Find the bulk modulus of the oil in units of $10^9\text{ N/m}^2$.
questions.solution:
Bulk modulus $B$ is given by:
$$B = \frac{\Delta P}{|\Delta V| / V_0} = \frac{2.0 \times 10^7}{\frac{5.0 \times 10^{-3}}{0.5}} = \frac{2.0 \times 10^7}{1.0 \times 10^{-2}} = 2.0 \times 10^9\text{ N/m}^2$$
Thus, the value in units of $10^9\text{ N/m}^2$ is $2.0$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] A copper wire of length $2.2\text{ m}$ and a steel wire of length $1.6\text{ m}$, both of diameter $3.0\text{ mm}$, are connected end to end to form a composite wire of total length $3.8\text{ m}$. When stretched by a load, the net elongation is $0.7\text{ mm}$. If $Y_{\text{copper}} = 1.1 \times 10^{11}\text{ N/m}^2$ and $Y_{\text{steel}} = 2.0 \times 10^{11}\text{ N/m}^2$, find the elongation of the copper segment in millimetres (rounded to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
Both wires have identical cross-sectional area $A$ and sustain identical tensile force $F$:
$$\Delta L_{\text{Cu}} = \frac{F L_{\text{Cu}}}{A Y_{\text{Cu}}}, \quad \Delta L_{\text{St}} = \frac{F L_{\text{St}}}{A Y_{\text{St}}}$$
$$\frac{\Delta L_{\text{Cu}}}{\Delta L_{\text{St}}} = \frac{L_{\text{Cu}} Y_{\text{St}}}{L_{\text{St}} Y_{\text{Cu}}} = \frac{2.2 \times (2.0 \times 10^{11})}{1.6 \times (1.1 \times 10^{11})} = \frac{4.4}{1.76} = 2.5$$
$$\Delta L_{\text{Cu}} = 2.5 \Delta L_{\text{St}}$$
Total elongation:
$$\Delta L_{\text{Cu}} + \Delta L_{\text{St}} = 0.7\text{ mm} \implies 2.5 \Delta L_{\text{St}} + \Delta L_{\text{St}} = 0.7 \implies 3.5 \Delta L_{\text{St}} = 0.7$$
$$\Delta L_{\text{St}} = 0.2\text{ mm} \implies \Delta L_{\text{Cu}} = 0.5\text{ mm}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A metal cube of side $10\text{ cm}$ has its bottom face rigidly fastened to the floor. A tangential force of $10^5\text{ N}$ is applied to its upper face. If the shear modulus of the material is $1.0 \times 10^{10}\text{ N/m}^2$, find the horizontal displacement (in $\mu\text{m}$) of the upper edge.
questions.solution:
Side of cube $L = 10\text{ cm} = 0.1\text{ m}$.
Area of the top face $A = L^2 = (0.1)^2 = 0.01\text{ m}^2 = 10^{-2}\text{ m}^2$.
Shear stress:
$$\tau = \frac{F}{A} = \frac{10^5}{10^{-2}} = 10^7\text{ N/m}^2$$
Shear strain $\theta$ is related to shear displacement $\Delta x$ by $\theta = \frac{\Delta x}{L}$:
$$\theta = \frac{\tau}{\eta} = \frac{10^7}{1.0 \times 10^{10}} = 10^{-3}$$
Horizontal displacement:
$$\Delta x = \theta L = 10^{-3} \times 0.1\text{ m} = 10^{-4}\text{ m} = 100 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m} = 100.0\,\mu\text{m}$$
